description: Operational dashboard for FMA launcher health, actuation latency, controller pressure, HTTP failures, and optional DCGM GPU framebuffer diagnostics. Empty DCGM panels mean those metrics are not available; they are not FMA health failures.

panels.description: Server-requesting Pods currently known to the dual-pods controller.
panels.title: Requesters

panels.description: Distinct requester Pods with an asserted FMA requester-provider binding. A multi-GPU binding is counted once.
panels.title: Active bindings

panels.description: All launcher Pods for the selected LauncherConfig values and phases.
panels.title: Launcher Pods

panels.description: Launchers that exceeded the configured scheduling or starting threshold. Any non-zero value requires investigation.
panels.title: Stuck launchers

panels.description: Fraction of controller-to-requester, launcher, and vLLM HTTP calls that did not return a 2xx status over the current rate interval. Status 0 means no HTTP response was received.
panels.title: HTTP error ratio

panels.description: UP only when both the dual-pods-controller and launcher-populator have discovered Prometheus targets and every matching target is healthy.

targets.expr: (min(up{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~".*dual-pods-controller.*"}) or vector(0)) * (min(up{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~".*launcher-populator.*"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Controller targets

panels.description: Completed actuation latency from requester container start through readiness relay. Failed or incomplete actuations are not observed by this histogram; correlate gaps with the HTTP and controller rows.
panels.title: Actuation latency by path

panels.description: Rate of completed cold, warm, and hot actuations. A drop to zero while requesters increase is a useful failure signal.
panels.title: Actuations / second

panels.description: Distribution of completed actuation paths in the selected dashboard time range. A lower hot share may explain a latency regression but is not itself an error.
panels.title: Path mix

panels.description: Launcher population by lifecycle phase. stuck_scheduling points to placement/capacity trouble; stuck_starting points to image, runtime, device, or probe trouble; stale indicates an old launcher template.
panels.title: Launcher phase history

panels.description: Current launcher counts by LauncherConfig and phase.
panels.title: Current launcher phases

panels.description: P95 latency of the Kubernetes API call that creates a launcher Pod object. It does not include scheduling, image pull, or container startup.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, lcfg_name, success) (rate(fma_launcher_create_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", lcfg_name=~"$lcfg"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Launcher create API latency P95

panels.description: Current server-requesting Pod count by InferenceServerConfig, and InferenceServerConfig count by LauncherConfig.
panels.title: Workload objects

panels.description: Failed Kubernetes API calls to create launcher Pod objects. This does not detect launcher Pods that were created but later became stuck.
panels.title: Launcher create API failures / second

panels.description: Observed controller process restarts during the selected time range, inferred from process_start_time_seconds. Use pod logs to determine the reason.
panels.title: Controller restarts in range

panels.description: Non-2xx controller HTTP calls by purpose and status. Status 0 means transport failure or timeout. Sustained 409 create_instance responses can expose GPU discovery or capacity conflicts.
panels.title: HTTP failures / second

panels.description: P95 controller HTTP latency by operation. Compare relay, create, sleep, and wake paths to identify the slow external step.
panels.title: HTTP latency P95 by purpose

panels.description: Current number of items waiting in each node-local DPC inner queue.
panels.title: DPC inner queue depth

panels.description: P95 time from a unique node-local enqueue to dequeue. Rising values indicate worker backlog or retry pressure.
panels.title: DPC queue latency P95

panels.description: P95 time spent processing one node-local work item. Compare with queue latency to distinguish slow work from backlog.
panels.title: DPC work latency P95

panels.description: Rate of node-local work items that required retry. A spike usually accompanies an unavailable launcher, stopped instance, or external-call failure.
panels.title: DPC retries / second

panels.description: All controller HTTP calls by purpose and method. This supplies context for both the error-ratio and latency panels.
panels.title: HTTP calls / second

panels.description: Total device framebuffer used on GPUs with an active FMA binding. This is GPU-level DCGM data joined through fma_duality; it is not per-process memory attribution and may repeat when multiple FMA instances share a GPU.
panels.title: GPU framebuffer used on FMA-bound devices

panels.description: Framebuffer utilization for GPUs with an active FMA binding. Sustained high usage before create_instance or wake failures is consistent with the observed CUDA OOM flake class. This remains device-level, not per-process attribution.

targets.expr: 100 * ((fma_duality{namespace=~"$namespace", node=~"$node"} == 1) * on (UUID) group_left max by (UUID) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED)) / on (UUID) group_left() (max by (UUID) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED) + max by (UUID) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_FREE))

panels.title: GPU framebuffer utilization on FMA-bound devices

panels.description: Current requester-to-launcher-to-instance-to-GPU relationships asserted by the dual-pods controller. One row is emitted per GPU in a multi-GPU instance.
panels.title: Active binding topology

title: FMA Operations
